Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing with pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
ideas.description: Like words in the list that share roots and prefixes (prewelcome, reimpose, exaugurate), cells sharing a heritable 'root' can be tracked by a lineage barcode. Split barcoded clonal populations into sister aliquots, profile one by scRNA-seq before drug and treat the other, then see whether the surviving barcodes already carried a distinct pre-existing transcriptional state, which distinguishes heritable/pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance.

ideas.title: Live-cell single-cell time-lapse with fate-mapping reporters
ideas.description: Track thousands of individual cells by long-term microscopy before and after drug using reporters for cell-cycle state, ERK/AKT signaling, apoptosis and stress. Retrospectively align pre-treatment dynamics, such as pulse frequency or cycle length, with eventual survival, like reading a sequence backward to find which earlier features predict the outcome.

ideas.title: Multi-omic profiling of persisters over time (scRNA + scATAC + histone marks)
ideas.description: Collect cells at several timepoints (untreated, days after drug, regrowth) and measure chromatin accessibility, key histone modifications (e.g., H3K27me3, KDM5 targets) and transcripts in the same cells. This tests whether survival reflects reversible epigenetic states, much like a long sequence of distinct tokens where only the arrangement of marks, not the underlying genome, differs.

ideas.title: Metabolic and stress-state measurements of survivors
ideas.description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes, ROS/lipid peroxidation sensors and drug efflux/accumulation assays sorted by flow to compare surviving and dying cells. Then test causality by perturbing the identified pathway (e.g., GPX4, OXPHOS, ABC transporters) to see whether the persister fraction changes.

ideas.title: Pooled CRISPR screens plus mathematical modeling of switching rates
ideas.description: Run genome-wide or targeted CRISPRi/a screens under drug to find genes that raise or lower persister frequency, and use fluctuation-test (Luria–Delbrück-style) assays to estimate rates of switching into and out of the tolerant state. Fit stochastic models to determine whether the survival fraction is explained by pre-existing rare states, noisy induced adaptation, or both.
